description: Every active Security Hub control failure (CIS 3.0.0 and FSBP) is remediated or in the exception record, each exception with its reason and a review date not yet passed; the pass rate across evaluated controls is recorded. Disabled controls are recorded in securityhub_controls.tf

exceptions.reason: Session keys (database until 2026-10-02, secrets, logs) are scheduled for deletion at every teardown by design: they encrypt what the teardown destroys. The persistent keys are carved out, so one of them scheduled for deletion fails.
Object-level write events are logged for the customer-data store only, by the 2026-09-05 MLA-LET cost decision; the trail's selectors are checked by mla-let-cfg-aws-trail-data-events-scoped.
Object-level read events: as S3.22, the 2026-09-05 MLA-LET decision.
There are no EC2 instances or EKS clusters: the workloads run on Fargate, and posture.tf records the EC2 and EKS add-ons as deliberately off (EKS audit logs).
There are no EC2 instances or EKS clusters: the workloads run on Fargate, and posture.tf records the EC2 and EKS add-ons as deliberately off (EKS runtime).

There are no EC2 instances or EKS clusters: the workloads run on Fargate, and posture.tf records the EC2 and EKS add-ons as deliberately off (Inspector EC2 scanning has nothing to scan).
Endpoints are declared per service the tasks call (network.tf, endpoint_actions); nothing calls the EC2 API from the VPC.
Endpoints are declared per service the tasks call; Systems Manager is not used.
Endpoints are declared per service the tasks call; Systems Manager Incident Manager Contacts is not used.
Endpoints are declared per service the tasks call; Systems Manager Incident Manager is not used.
Nothing here uses SSM Automation; there are no runbooks to log. Decided 2026-10-03.
The operator reaches AWS Support through an elevation (ElevatedAdmin, elevation.tf); a separate support role would be a second identity for a two-person team. Decided 2026-10-03.
Detection reads the trail from S3 through Athena and the normalized corpus, not CloudWatch Logs; integrating it would duplicate the stream and its cost. Decided 2026-10-03.

Server access logging is not enabled: customer-data object access is recorded as CloudTrail data events (the 2026-09-05 MLA-LET scope), and the other buckets hold logs, state and scratch output. Decided 2026-10-03.
As S3.9, for the trail's own bucket: its writes are CloudTrail's, and reads of it are confined to four declared readers by bucket policy. Decided 2026-10-03.
MFA delete can be set only by the root user through the API. The log store's Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode is stronger: nobody can delete a locked version, root included. Decided 2026-10-03.
The one customer-data store holds synthetic measurements, classified by design; Macie bills per bucket and per byte scanned for a classification the design already made. Decided 2026-10-03.
The two Lambdas are first-party code using only the runtime's boto3, with no packaged dependencies to scan; their source is reviewed in the repository. Decided 2026-10-03.
As Inspector.3: no packaged dependencies. Decided 2026-10-03.

Runtime Monitoring is not enabled, decided 2026-10-07 rather than trialled: on Fargate GuardDuty creates its own VPC endpoint and security group inside the session VPC, outside Terraform, which can block teardown.sh from deleting the VPC and would fail the declared-inventory checks, and it bills after the trial. Threat detection stands on CloudTrail, VPC flow, DNS, S3, RDS and Lambda signals; process-level observation is the recorded gap on CNA-DFP validate 3.

Threat detection stands on CloudTrail, VPC flow, DNS, S3, RDS and Lambda signals; process-level observation is the recorded gap on CNA-DFP validate 3.

Config records the 17 types the inventory reconciles, not every type an enabled control covers: Config bills per configuration item and the environment is rebuilt every session (DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-05). The control's other half, the service-linked role, is remediated (2026-10-03). Decided 2026-10-05.

Load balancer deletion protection would block teardown.sh, which destroys the application environment after every session by design (DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-22). The environment is rebuilt from declared state in about 15 minutes. Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

Database deletion protection would block teardown.sh likewise. The data's protection is its retained backups under the persistent database key, and the point-in-time restore measured at 15.7 minutes (2026-10-06). Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

Multi-AZ doubles the instance cost for a database that stands only during sessions; the recorded availability position is a single zone, recovered by point-in-time restore against a 60-minute objective (registers/resources.yaml). Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

Enhanced monitoring needs a monitoring role carrying the AWS-managed AmazonRDSEnhancedMonitoringRole policy, which the CNA-DFP decision of 2026-09-05 bars on workload identities. Database logs go to CloudWatch under the logs key. Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

Moving off 5432 is obscurity only: three security groups confine the port to the api, worker and migrate tasks, and the database is private with IAM authentication (registers/flows.yaml). Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

The one failing secret, the task TLS key, is generated afresh at every apply of the environment, so it never outlives the session that uses it -- shorter than any rotation schedule (registers/secrets.yaml). The database credential is RDS-managed and rotates. Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.

Container Insights is off by a recorded decision: it bills per metric, and the environment's operational health is covered by the alarms in health.tf (compute.tf). Turning it on would also create an undeclared, unencrypted, never-expiring log group. Decided 2026-10-06; evaluated only while the session environment stands.
